reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-4 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: A rectangle has sides 11 cm and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 9 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 9 cm and 6 cm. What is its perimeter?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: I recomputed perimeter as 2*(length+width) for every seed (e.g. 11+2 doubled is 26, 7+9 doubled is 32) and every stated correct_answer matches exactly, so the core perimeter arithmetic is sound for the rectangle case.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: This competency explicitly names three shapes (triangles, squares, and rectangles) but all 7 seeds (42-48) render only rectangles with two distinct side lengths -- no triangle or square perimeter item appears anywhere in the sample.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The single-sentence stem 'A rectangle has sides X cm and Y cm. What is its perimeter?' is straightforward for grade-2 quarter-4 readers who have already met basic shape vocabulary.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Because squares are a degenerate rectangle case (equal sides) and triangles require a third side value entirely, their complete absence from this 7-seed sample suggests the variant space may not actually generate those two of the three named shapes.

competency_alignment.rationale: Content correctly targets 'find the perimeter of ... rectangles' but as sampled gives no evidence of covering the 'triangles' and 'squares' clauses that are equally part of this lc's explicit wording.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Side lengths of 1-11 cm producing perimeters up to 32 cm are well within grade-2 quarter-4 arithmetic capability (simple two-digit addition doubled).
